item.title: Managing Intellectual Property and Intangible Assets across the Lifecycle of Circular or Regenerative Innovation
item.content:encoded:
Frank Tietze, University of Cambridge

Dolores Modic, Nord University

Giovanna Capponi, Utrecht University

Pratheeba Vimalnath, University of Exeter

Ioana Stefan, Mälardalen University

This special issue examines intellectual property and intangible asset management in circular and regenerative innovation. As organizations transition from linear to circular business models, IP management becomes critical because these innovations require intangible assets to flow across organizational boundaries, enabling collaborative value creation. IP rights present tensions: they can incentivize circular R&D and govern collaborations, yet also limit technology access, restrict innovation diffusion, or reinforce linear models.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and empirical research from innovation management, circular economy, and IP perspectives. It addresses how IP management can enable or constrain transitions toward circularity and regeneration across product and technology lifecycles. The editors invite solution-oriented contributions, interdisciplinary work, and research spanning diverse sectors, firm sizes, and countries, including low- and middle-income economies.

Appel publié par R and D Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Alignment between IP strategy, business strategy and circular/regenerative objectives
  • CE/RE-specific IP and intangible asset management approaches
  • Strategic use of IP by innovation ecosystem stakeholders towards CE/RE transitions
  • Factors affecting degree of openness and associated IP strategies for CE/RE
  • Soft IP for collaborative innovation (data, software, algorithms, know-how)
  • IP sharing models and licensing approaches for ecosystem collaboration
  • IP support systems for start-ups and SMEs in coopetition settings
  • Advancing IP skills and capabilities for collaborative CE/RE innovation
  • IP regimes, institutional frameworks and innovation policies for CE/RE
  • Geopolitical shifts, supply-chain dependencies and IP provisions in trade agreements
  • Evolving legislation and its impact on firm-level IP strategies (rights to repair)
  • Patent, trademark and novel datasets for measuring CE/RE innovation
  • GenAI and LLMs for new research designs on IP and innovation
  • Interdisciplinary approaches to IP governance combining multiple perspectives
  • Case study methodologies for IP impacts on R&D and innovation management
